conventions.convention: A curve is geometrically integral, separated, finite type over its field, and of chain dimension one. Smoothness and properness are additional hypotheses.
Curve divisors are finite sums of closed points; degree is the sum of coefficients weighted by residue-field degrees.
L(D) contains zero and the nonzero rational functions satisfying div(f)+D≥0; positive coefficients permit poles.
Complete linear systems initially mean sets of effective divisors, identified with k-lines in L(D); these sets are distinguished from projective parameter schemes.
Section vanishing at x means ord_x(f)+n_x≥1. The zero subspace has every closed point as a base point. For target P⁰ a nonzero linear form defines the empty hyperplane.
Differential orders use coefficients in local frames, not necessarily differentials of uniformizers. Inseparable residue extensions are allowed.

Index-unramified means e=1; scheme-theoretic unramifiedness additionally requires a separable residue extension. The different uses lengths of the full relative differentials only for generically separable maps.
Geometric genus through smooth normalization is defined here over perfect fields; delta invariants and their genus correction are stated over algebraically closed fields.
Approximation guarantees are value inequalities: minimization uses factor ρ≥1 and maximization factor 0<ρ≤1. Zero optima are included without division.
Weighted set-cover costs are nonnegative rationals, the listed sets cover the universe, ties use the smallest input index, and H₀=0.
Metric TSP has at least three vertices, a complete graph, nonnegative symmetric rational lengths, zero diagonal, and the triangle inequality; tours include the closing edge.

Gap scales are positive; zero-clause formulas are outside the gap domains. Clause graphs retain repeated literal occurrences. APX-hardness is explicitly defined using L-reductions and is not inferred from no-PTAS results.
The boundary is R/Z identified with the unit circle, with normalized Haar probability measure on its Borel sigma-algebra; complex harmonicity is componentwise.
Centered arcs have measure 2h; the h=1/2 arc is the whole circle including the antipode. Maximal averages use total variation. Cones satisfy |z−ζ|<A(1−|z|), A>1.
Finite-p radial convergence is in Lp; the infinity endpoint asserts weak-star convergence against bilinear L¹ tests, not L∞ norm convergence. h¹ boundary measures need not have densities.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a smooth curve C over a field k and a closed point x, O_C,x is a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension one, hence a discrete valuation ring with a uniformizer; nonzero rational functions have integer orders and nonzero local elements are units times uniformizer powers.

Assume AC together with inherited DC. On a smooth proper geometrically integral curve, closed-point local rings are DVRs and the generic local ring is a field, so the curve is locally factorial; the Cartier-to-Weil cycle map is an isomorphism compatible with principal divisors; Cartier divisors modulo principal divisors identify with Pic, and every invertible sheaf is O(D), with D determined modulo linear equivalence.

Assume AC. For an integral separated finite-type curve over k, the affine integral closures in its function field are finite and commute with principal localization. They glue to an integral normal scheme with a finite affine birational map, the same function field, and initiality among normal integral schemes finite and birational over the curve, hence uniqueness up to unique isomorphism over it.

Assume AC. For a proper curve over k that is geometrically connected and geometrically reduced, the canonical map k→H⁰(C,O_C) is an isomorphism. For a proper integral curve, H⁰(C,O_C) is a finite field extension of k; it equals k under the stated geometric hypotheses, hence for every proper curve under this page's geometrically integral convention.

Assume AC. For a finite surjective map of smooth proper geometrically integral curves with finite separable function-field extension, Ω_C/D is coherent torsion with finite support. Its local length l_p satisfies l_p≥e_p−1; l_p=0 iff e_p=1 and the residue extension is separable; l_p=e_p−1 iff the residue extension is separable and e_p is invertible in the target residue field. Otherwise l_p≥e_p. Its support is precisely the points with e_p>1 or inseparable residue extension.
Assume AC. For a nonconstant morphism f:C→D of smooth proper geometrically integral curves of degree n and a closed point q of D, the fibre is finite and Σ_{p∈f⁻¹(q)} e_p[κ(p):κ(q)]=n.
Assume AC and algebraically closed k. For an integral proper finite-type curve X with normalization X^nu, p_a(X)=g(X^nu)+Σ_x δ_x(X); the sum is finite and supported on singular points.

Assume AC for the published PCP supplier proof route. For every language L in NP, its perfect-completeness binary PCP verifier with constantly many nonadaptive queries, logarithmically many fair random bits and fixed soundness s<1 yields a deterministic polynomial-time map x↦F_x with M≥1 clauses and fixed δ>0: yes inputs have Max-3SAT optimum M; no inputs have optimum at most (1−δ)M.

Every 3-CNF formula with m clauses of three literal occurrences yields in polynomial time a simple occurrence graph with 3m vertices and α(G)=OPT_Max3SAT(F). The positive-scale m versus (1−δ)m promise transfers unchanged for m≥1 and 0<δ≤1. The empty formula gives an empty graph and both optima zero. An independent set of size k decodes in polynomial time to an assignment satisfying at least k clauses.

Assume countable choice. For 1≤p≤∞ and f∈Lp(T,m;C), P[f] is complex harmonic, lies in h^p, and ||P_r*f||p≤||f||p for 0≤r<1. For finite p, ||P_r*f−f||p→0 as r↑1. No general L∞ norm convergence is asserted.

Assume AC. Every h¹ function is P[μ] for a unique finite regular complex Borel measure μ on T; conversely every such measure gives an h¹ function, with ||P[μ]||h¹=|μ|(T). Its radial density measures converge weak-star to μ against C(T). A general h¹ boundary measure need not have an L¹ density.
Assume countable choice. For every finite regular complex Borel measure μ, A>1 and ζ∈T, N_A(P[μ])(ζ)≤(A+1)² M_T μ(ζ); in particular the corresponding inequality holds for every L¹ density.

Assume countable choice. For f∈L¹(T,m;C), P[f](z)→f(ζ) for almost every ζ as z→ζ within every fixed cone Γ_A(ζ), A>1. The assertion uses an almost-everywhere representative and makes no claim about arbitrary tangential paths.

concerns.concern: The Statement allows any proper k-scheme Y, but def-rational-map-integral-schemes defines rational maps only when Y is integral and finite type. Nonintegral proper targets therefore fall outside the cited definition. The extension argument works with the usual broader definition, but that interface is not supplied.

Statement and Proof 5.1 say AC is used 'exactly' through the DVR criterion and that remaining inputs are choice-free. However F2's def-smooth-morphism-to-field-classical and F3's lem-affine-local-dimension-residue-transcendence explicitly assume AC. The overall AC hypothesis is present; its exact-use accounting is inaccurate.

Neither Statement nor Given assumes AC, while both proof suppliers, thm-plane-curve-arithmetic-genus and lem-normalization-lowers-arithmetic-genus-delta, explicitly require it. No alternative choice-free argument is supplied.

Example says 'over every other point of P¹_k there lie two points with e_p=1'. This includes the generic point as written. Its fibre is Spec k(C), a single point with a degree-two field extension; e_p is defined here only for closed points. Verification 5.1 correctly restricts the assertion to closed points.

F2 states 'a point of a curve is smooth exactly when its local ring is regular', without perfectness or geometric regularity. That general equivalence fails over imperfect fields. For example, over k=F_p(a), p odd, y²=x^p−a is geometrically integral and has a regular DVR at (y), but becomes singular after adjoining a^(1/p). The fixed conic is already assumed smooth, so the proof does not need this overstrong converse.

F6 assigns dim_{κ(q)}(M) to every finite A-module of finite length. Finite length alone does not make the A-action factor through κ(q)=A/m_A; a module with nonzero uniformizer action lacks that induced residue-field vector-space structure. The actual fibre algebra is annihilated by m_A, so the proof's application can be justified with that narrower hypothesis.

The 'More precisely' clause uses one fixed δ to conclude that a fixed-factor algorithm decides every NP language. The preceding lemma obtains δ from the chosen language's verifier, whereas Proof 4.2 repeats the argument for arbitrary L. The uniform conclusion needs the short additional route through one fixed NP-complete language and its reductions.

Proof 1.1 establishes radial L¹ bounds for P[μ] and then concludes membership in h¹ without establishing harmonicity for measure data. The definition only establishes well-definedness, and the earlier harmonicity theorem treats Lp densities. Differentiating the kernel under the finite-variation integral on compact subdiscs supplies the missing elementary justification.

Proof 2.1 writes '|P[μ](0)|=|μ|(T)'. For a complex measure the left side is |μ(T)|, which may be strictly smaller than total variation: μ=δ_a−δ_b with a≠b gives 0 versus 2. The desired bound still follows from |μ(T)|≤|μ|(T), but the displayed equality is false.

Proof 5.1–6.1 uses strict inequalities for every compact K in the superlevel set. If μ=0, the set and K are empty, the selected family is empty, and the written strict inequality becomes 0<0. The theorem remains immediate in this case; the proof needs an empty-family or zero-measure branch.

Verification 2.3 identifies '{s∈[0,1):d([s],[0])<h}' with '(-h,h)'. These are different subsets of R; the first is [0,h)∪(1−h,1). The resulting integral over (−h,h) is valid by periodicity and a change of fundamental interval, which should replace the false set equality.

alerts.finding: F3 says 'The complete linear system |L| is base-point-free of dimension h⁰(C,L)=r+1' while the same paragraph sets r=h⁰(C,L)−1 and cites thm-base-point-free-linear-system-morphism. The vector space of sections has dimension r+1; its projective linear system has dimension r. In this item's h⁰=3 case, |L| has dimension two.

seams_checked.note: Checked current supplier clauses for O(D), principal and effective divisors, rational sections, cycle maps, Picard degree, and finite function maps. Consumers preserve the pole-permitting O(D) sign, normal/Noetherian/integral hypotheses, residue weights, and AC→DC premises. Rational sections are not asserted regular for arbitrary signed divisors.

DVR, canonical-bundle, L(D), fibre-degree and different uses otherwise preserve their hypotheses; local uniformizer differential claims add separable residues, and Riemann–Hurwitz retains generic separability. One citing Fact changes the linear-system dimension: cor-degree-three-line-bundle-embeds-genus-one-plane-cubic F3 calls |L| dimension h⁰ rather than h⁰−1; routed in alerts.

Checked current citing paragraphs for curve definitions, L(D)=H⁰(O(D)), scalar-orbit systems, DVRs, Cartier–Weil comparison, H⁰(O)=k, effective degree, finite function maps and degree-one isomorphisms. They retain geometric integrality, closed-point residue weights, and explicit AC premises.
